news.title: That Virus Alert Popup Is a Scam — Microsoft Never Puts a Phone Number in a Warning
news.excerpt: Fake virus popups blast a siren and a phone number. Microsoft, Apple, and Google never put phone numbers in warnings. Close the browser tab. If it won't close, hold the power button 15 seconds. Source: FTC.gov, Microsoft Support

news.title: Fake Adobe Update Scams Exploit Real November Security Patches
news.excerpt:
Adobe just released its November 2026 security patches across nine product families including Photoshop, Acrobat, and Creative Cloud. Scammers know this and are pushing fake "Adobe update" pop-ups and emails that look identical to the real thing — same logos, same wording, same urgency. Clicking them installs malicious code instead of the actual patch.

What to do: Never update Adobe apps from a pop-up or email link. Open the Creative Cloud desktop app directly, or go to adobe.com and sign in to check for updates. Real Adobe updates never come through browser pop-ups.

news.title: Accidental Payment Scam: Don't Send Money Back
news.excerpt:
You get an unexpected payment — Venmo, Cash App, Zelle, or a text
message says someone sent you money by mistake. Then a message follows:
"They accidentally sent you money, please send it back." If you send it
back, you lose. The original payment may be fraudulent and get reversed
by the bank, but the money you voluntarily sent is gone for good.

What to do: Do not send money back. Leave the funds untouched and
contact your bank or payment service through its official app, website,
or customer-service number. Do not trust screenshots or messages from
the sender as proof. Avoid clicking links from strangers — they lead to
fake login pages.

This matters: Scammers use stolen cards or hacked accounts to send the
initial payment. When the real owner disputes it, the bank reverses...

news.title: CISA adds four new actively exploited vulnerabilities to catalog — patch GPUStack, FreeSwitch, OpenSSH, Aspera now
news.excerpt: CISA added four new actively exploited vulnerabilities on November 9: GPUStack (CVE-2026-102895), SignalWire FreeSwitch (CVE-2026-116779), OpenBSD OpenSSH (CVE-2026-123158), and IBM Aspera Faspex (CVE-2026-123218). Check the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog at cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog and update any affected software immediately.

posts.title: Windows Quick Assist Gives Free Remote Help — No Third-Party Tool Needed
posts.summary: Windows Quick Assist (built into Windows 10 and 11) lets someone you trust see your screen and help fix problems. Open Start, search Quick Assist, click "Help someone" and share the code. Free, no install
posts.truth: I've seen people pay $100+ for "remote support" scams when Windows has had this built in since 2016. The scammer asks you to install TeamViewer or AnyDesk — Quick Assist needs zero downloads.

posts.title: Clay Electric Outage Texts Tell You the Power Is Out Before Your Neighbor Knows — Free Signup
posts.summary: Sign up free at clayelectric.com for outage texts and the live outage map at clayelectric.outagemap.coop — covers Columbia County and Lake City
posts.truth: Every storm season someone loses a computer to a power surge because they didn't know the power was flickering. A $30 surge strip and outage alerts cost less than a motherboard.

posts.title: CISA Confirms 18 New Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities This Week — Free Patch List at cisa.gov
posts.summary: CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog added 18 new vulnerabilities in the last 7 days. Check if you run OSGeo GeoServer, Drupal, Mitel MiCollab, or Danfoss AK-SM — patch immediately free at cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
posts.truth: Most people think "I'm too small to be a target." The automated scanners don't care — they hit every IP address. If you run a vulnerable service on the internet, it's not a matter of if, it's when.

posts.title: Microsoft Defender now discovers local AI agents running on your PC — free and built into Windows 11
posts.summary: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage settings. Microsoft Defender automatically detects 50+ local AI agents like Ollama, LM Studio, and Jan and shows their configured model connections — no setup needed.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize their AI chat apps are visible to Windows security. This is a good thing — it means Defender can flag if something suspicious starts running.

posts.title: CISA warns SharePoint servers under active attack — patch CVE-2026-65660 and CVE-2026-67279 now
posts.summary: Apply the November 2026 Microsoft security update via Windows Update or the Microsoft Update Catalog — it patches the actively exploited SharePoint code injection and SSH workflow flaws.

posts.title: Deleted a File by Mistake? Recuva Recovers It Free — No Tech Skills Needed
posts.summary: Recuva (ccleaner.com/recuva) is the free Windows tool that recovers deleted photos, documents, and files from hard drives, USB sticks, and memory cards. Works on Windows 10 and 11
posts.truth: People panic and keep using the drive — that overwrites the deleted data and makes recovery impossible. Stop using the drive the second you realize a file is gone.

posts.title: Firefox 160 address bar now shows Paste and Search when you paste a search term — free update at firefox.com
posts.summary: Update Firefox to 160 via Menu > Help > About Firefox. Copy any text, click the address bar, and paste — Firefox now offers "Paste and Search" instead of "Paste and Go" when it detects a search term rather than a URL.
posts.truth: This is one of those small quality-of-life changes that makes you wonder how you lived without it. Stop copying, clicking search engine, pasting — just paste and search.

posts.title: Ventoy puts every ISO on one USB — free multi-boot tool at ventoy.net beats reformatting every time
posts.summary: Download Ventoy at ventoy.net, run it on your USB drive, then drag and drop ISO files — no reformatting needed.
posts.truth: I used to carry a bag of USB drives for every Windows version and Linux distro — now one Ventoy drive does it all.
